title: Penalties & Points
whatItIs: Penalty points (endorsements) go on your driving record when you break certain traffic laws. Too many and you lose your licence.
keyFacts: If you get 12 or more points within 3 years, you can be banned from driving.
New drivers: 6 or more points within 2 years of passing and your licence is revoked.
Points stay on your driving record for 4 or 11 years, depending on the offence.
Using a hand-held phone while driving: £200 and 6 points.
Speeding usually means at least 3 points, and can mean up to 6.

onTheTest.question: You passed your test a year ago. How many points would get your licence revoked?
onTheTest.why: If you get 6 or more points within 2 years of passing your test, your licence is revoked.

traps: 12 points is the limit for experienced drivers. New drivers lose their licence at 6.
Drink-driving endorsements stay on your record for 11 years.
Points are counted over 3 years, not one calendar year.
